This land is not mine — I rent this small piece, so I will not put too much money into it. Cassava and cocoyam do not need fertilizer like maize does, and here in the South South the soil still gives something if I add the old manure from the small goats and kitchen ash. I will plant the cassava cuttings I saved from last year's harvest, like my mother did, because the improved stems from the agro-dealer cost money I do not have this season. The weeds grow fast with our rain, so I will weed by hand with my daughter — I cannot waste money on chemicals for such a small plot.
